newsitem.title: JAPAN: Monetary policy shouldn't stress stable forex -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Monetary policy shouldn't stress stable forex -- BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a parliamentary committee on Thursday that monetary policy should not put too much emphasis on such things as stabilising exchange rates and redressing external imbalances.
"I think it would be a problem to put too much emphasis on such things as stabilising exchange rates and redressing external imbalances," Matsushita said.

He added that the central bank attaches importance to money supply movements along with price movements in forming its monetary policy, although controlling the money supply is not in itself the goal of the monetary policy.

Asked about the BOJ's role in triggering the bubble economy of inflated stock and land prices in the late 1980s, Matsushita said he could not deny that an easy credit stance implemented over a long period had played a part.
He said he would like to learn from this past experience and act appropriately in forming Japan's monetary policy.
